_doc: Textes du catalogue des FANZZY (assets/fanzzy/fanzzy.json) : familles, séries, histoires et cris. Les noms des FANZZY restent en français.
ceux qui reviennent chaque samedi: the ones who come back every Saturday
ceux qui font tourner la baraque: the ones who keep the place running
neuf cents kilomètres, et ça commence ma: nine hundred kilometres, and it's off to a bad start
debout sous le crachin, et le thé a déjà: standing in the drizzle, and the tea has already gone cold
Onze ans, une parka trop grande, et l’ai: Eleven years old, a parka two sizes too big, and the look of someone who's been let down before. He knows the chants before the words.
Il loue des transats sur une promenade o: He rents out deckchairs on a promenade where it rains nine days out of ten. He shouts about them anyway, in time with the waves — and on the tenth day, he's right.
Annoncé sur le quai, deux minutes avant: Announced on the platform, two minutes before departure. Thirty people in shirts stare at the same board in disbelief.
Elle remonte la grande rue des boutiques: She walks up the high street in her uniform, the blue leather jacket folded over her arm: she doesn't dare wear it yet. In her Walkman, a borrowed tape, and her foot tapping the beat without her noticing.
Onze ans, une caisse claire trop grande: Eleven years old, a snare drum too big for him, and the look of someone entrusted with a state mission.
À la sortie du parking, avant même d’avo: At the car park exit, before even reaching the motorway. The spare wheel is under the scarves and the scarves are under everything else.
Sa banderole est vide. Il attend le bon: His banner is blank. He's waiting for the right night to write on it, and the right night hasn't come for three seasons.
Trop jeune pour entrer, il attend sur le: Too young to go in, he waits on the pavement for his dad to finish his pint. He watches the painted sign creak in the wind, and copies it onto everything he finds.
Il pose les avis de déplacement la nuit,: He puts up the away-trip notices at night, hood up, one eye over his shoulder. The posters are blank: he's never done anything wrong.
La personne la plus ordinaire de la trib: The most ordinary person in the stand, and the one who's always there. Hands in pockets, flask in the other.
Il était venu visiter la vieille fortere: He came to visit the old fortress on a day with no match. A raven landed on his shoulder and never left: since then, they go to the stadium together, with a bag of crumbs.
Trois heures du matin, une cabine, et un: Three in the morning, a toll booth, and a coach full of singing fans. He lifts the barrier without opening his eyes.
Écharpe remontée sur le nez, torche étei: Scarf pulled up over his nose, unlit torch in his fist, he waits for the exact minute. Nothing is lit yet, and that's the whole point.
Sur la plage de galets, elle suce un bât: On the pebble beach, she sucks a stick of striped rock longer than her hand. When they score, she throws all her sweets over the railing, and regrets it until half-time.
La grand-mère qui conduit quatre jeunes: The grandmother who drives four youngsters to the stadium in her little car. She knows every shortcut and never slows down.
Assis sur la porte de l’écluse, il regar: Sitting on the lock gate, he watched the painted barges go by, wondering where they were going. He found out one Saturday: to the away match, at six kilometres an hour.
Pouce levé, carton vierge sous le bras,: Thumb out, a blank sign under his arm, four hundred kilometres to go and not a worry about it.
Immobilisé sur la bande d’arrêt d’urgenc: Stuck on the hard shoulder a hundred and forty kilometres from the stadium. Nine people and only one idea of what to do.
